title: Frank Welch, Albert Batiste and meeting Celestin
summary: Ridgley says Frank Welch was his teacher and Albert Batiste was first cornet. Batiste connected them to Celestin, with whom they got together.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Learning your horn: teachers, lessons and fees

blocks.x: Yeah. Yeah. What about Frank Welch?
He used to be our teacher, Frank Welch.

After I left off of Jefferson Powers, came to New Orleans, and my friend played cornet with us. In the Washington area, too, with Albert Batiste. He was the first cornet player with us. And his boy Joe played drum. Is Joe still alive? The old man, no, he's been there. I think Joe is the ... the but I don't know whether he played music anymore or not. For that, his father and son, he used to play. But that's ... and he's a fine old musician, too. Old man, wacky work. Joe's going to play with him and his boy Joe played drums.

The old man, no he's been there. I think Joe is there, but I don't know whether he played music anymore or not. I think he'd give it up. Well that's his father and son used to play. But that's, and he's a fine old musician too. Old man, where I go.
Did he play with other bands that you know of?

He played at other bands before he played with me. And he played with Bill and Terry Brass bands and things. He played with them. He played lots of bands in the city. Lots of jobs. He's a fine old man. And he was the one that connected us with Celestine, Frank Wilson. He was playing cornet and he did more plays. And he knew Celestine and he told us in Civil East band about Celestine. We went to see him and we got him. That's how we got together. Now, Emanuel Perez, is that right? Is it Perez? No. Yeah, he was a cornet player.
